analysis: The closest option anchors its breadth in all five Philosophy offerings, political philosophy, philosophical human rights and formal logic. Archaeology and history add evidence on citizenship, hierarchy and ideas about modernity, and literature and rhetoric add close reading and argument. This does not duplicate the chronological philosophical survey, advanced metaethics or epistemology. The second route builds normative inquiry through Ethics, Political Philosophy and Human Rights, alongside responsibility and punishment in Criminal Law, rights and authority in Constitutional Law, and legitimacy and institutions in EU law and politics. Social theory provides a distinct institutional and public dimension. The third route retains Mind, Emotion, Free Will and Ethics and develops the language and mind strand through Psycholinguistics, Perception & Action and Higher Order Functions. Logic and experimental methods support analysis. Machine Learning contributes empirical and computational methods, and AI Ethics directly examines agency and responsibility. Cognitive science does not substitute for a specialist philosophy of language sequence. All three make different substantial choices. The human-nature direction remains academically real and is recorded at the contractual maximum rather than approved as another option. Positive component matches reflect content overlap in ethics, mind, logic, political philosophy and introductory philosophical history. The specialised sequences, open and coherent electives, and required thesis retain distinct treatment.
